abacti: abigō, -ere, -ēgī, -āctum — to drive away, drive off course (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.; 'driven off')
absistere: absistō, -ere, -stitī — to stand off, give up, withdraw from (+ abl.) (pres. inf.)
accitos: acciō, -īre, -īvī, -ītum — to summon, send for (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl., with prīmōs)
actum: agō, -ere, ēgī, āctum — to do, drive, achieve (perf. pass. part., n. nom. sg.; nihil āctum, 'nothing was accomplished')
adpetii: appetō (adpetō), -ere, -īvī/-iī, -ītum — to strive for, attack, assail (1st sg. perf., = adpetīvī)
adscitis: adsciscō (ascīscō), -ere, -scīvī, -scītum — to take to oneself, adopt as allies (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. pl.)
adsidet: adsideō (assideō), -ēre, -sēdī — to sit beside; sit down before, besiege (3rd sg. pres.)
adsurgat: adsurgō (assurgō), -ere, -surrēxī — to rise up, rise to a blow (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
adusque: adusque (prep. + acc., adv.) — all the way to, right up to, as far as
aeneaeque: Aenēās, -ae (m.) — Aeneas, Trojan leader (gen. sg.) + -que, and
aequas: aequus, -a, -um — level, even; fair, equal (f. acc. pl., with lēgēs: 'even-handed terms')
aetola: Aetōlus, -a, -um — Aetolian, of Aetolia (Greek region; Diomedes' home, Arpi in Italy) (f. abl. sg., with urbe)

aliamque: alius, -a, -ud — other, another (f. acc. sg., with gentem) + -que, and
amicitiae: amīcitia, -ae (f.) — friendship, alliance (dat. sg., with cēdat)
amissi: āmittō, -ere, -mīsī, -missum — to lose, let go (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl., 'lost' companions)
antiquus: antīquus, -a, -um — old, ancient, long-held (m. nom. sg., with ager)
argyripam: Argyripa, -ae (f.) — Argyripa, the city Diomedes founded in Apulia, later Arpi (acc. sg., Greek form)
arpos: Arpī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Arpi, Apulian city, Diomedes' town (acc. pl.; with attraxerit)
atrides: Atrīdēs, -ae (m.) — son of Atreus; here Menelaus (nom. sg., Greek form; Agamemnon is also an Atrīdēs)
attraxerit: attrahō, -ere, -trāxī, -tractum — to draw to, bring (3rd sg. perf. subj., indirect question)
audisti: audiō, -īre, -īvī, -ītum — to hear (2nd sg. perf., contracted = audīvistī)
bellando: bellō, -āre — to wage war, fight (gerund, abl. sg., 'by fighting')
caelestia: caelestis, -e — heavenly, divine (n. acc. pl., with corpora)
caphareus: Caphareus, -eī (m.) — Caphareus, the rocky Euboean cape where Ajax's Greek fleet was wrecked (nom. sg.; with ultor)
cavete: caveō, -ēre, cāvī, cautum — to beware, take care (+ ut/ne or +acc.) (pl. imper.)
certatum: certō, -āre — to contend, fight (perf. pass. part., n. nom. sg., impersonal: certātum est, 'the struggle has been fought')
cessatum: cessō, -āre — to hold back, linger, be idle (perf. pass. part., impersonal: cessātum est, 'there was delay')
cogere: cōgō, -ere, coēgī, coāctum — to drive together, assemble, compel (pres. inf.)
complere: compleō, -ēre, -plēvī, -plētum — to fill, man, fill up (pres. inf.)
concurrant: concurrō, -ere, -currī, -cursum — to run together, clash (3rd pl. pres. subj., jussive)
considant: consīdō, -ere, -sēdī — to sit down, settle, take up residence (3rd pl. pres. subj., jussive)
consulite: cōnsulō, -ere, -suī, -sultum — to consult, take counsel; consulere in medium, deliberate for the common good (pl. imper.)
contigimusque: contingō, -ere, -tigī, -tactum — to touch, clasp (1st pl. perf.) + -que, and
contulimusque: cōnferō, -ferre, -tulī, collātum — to bring together; manūs cōnferre, to join battle (1st pl. perf.) + -que, and
crepitantibus: crepitō, -āre — to rattle, crackle, clatter, splash noisily (pres. part., f. abl. pl., with undīs)
decimum: decimus, -a, -um — tenth (m. acc. sg., with annum)
demus: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give, provide (1st pl. pres. subj., jussive)
denas: dēnī, -ae, -a — ten each, ten at a time; bis dēnās, twenty (f. acc. pl., with nāvīs)
devictam: dēvincō, -ere, -vīcī, -victum — to conquer completely, subdue (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg., with Asiam)
dicamus: dīcō, -ere, dīxī, dictum — to say; here to lay down, appoint (terms) (1st pl. pres. subj., jussive)
diomedem: Diomēdēs, -is (m.) — Diomedes, Greek hero at Troy, now founder of Argyripa in Apulia (acc. sg., Greek form -ēn)
diversum: dīversus, -a, -um — turned different ways, far apart, distant (n. acc. sg., with lītus)
docemus: doceō, -ēre, docuī, doctum — to teach, tell, make known (1st pl. pres.)
expendimus: expendō, -ere, -pendī, -pēnsum — to weigh out; pay (a penalty), suffer for (1st pl. pres.)
experto: experior, -īrī, expertus sum — to try, test; expertus, one who has tried (perf. part., m. dat. sg.; expertō crēdite, 'trust one who knows')
exsulat: exsulō, -āre — to live in exile, be banished (3rd sg. pres.)
farier: for, fārī, fātus sum — to speak, say (pres. inf. pass., archaic -ier form = fārī)
fatalem: fātālis, -e — fated, fateful, sent by fate (m. acc. sg., with Aenean)
firment: firmō, -āre — to make firm, ratify, confirm (3rd pl. pres. subj., in a purpose relative clause)
flagrante: flagrō, -āre — to blaze, burn, rage (pres. part., m./n. abl. sg., with tumultū)
fluuntque: fluō, -ere, flūxī — to flow, stream, pour (3rd pl. pres.) + -que, and
fortunatae: fortūnātus, -a, -um — fortunate, blessed, happy (f. voc. pl., with gentēs)
fuerunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd pl. perf., = fuērunt; with speranda, 'had to be expected')
gargani: Gārgānus, -ī (m.) — Mount Garganus, the promontory on Apulia's Adriatic coast (m. gen. sg., with agrīs)
gerimus: gerō, -ere, gessī, gestum — to carry, conduct; bellum gerere, to wage war (1st pl. pres.)
habitantis: habitō, -āre — to dwell, inhabit (pres. part., m. acc. pl., -is for -ēs, with Locrōs)
habuistis: habeō, -ēre, -uī, -itum — to have, hold (2nd pl. perf.)
horribili: horribilis, -e — dreadful, terrible, awe-inspiring (m./n. abl. sg.; horribilī vīsū, 'terrible to see')
horum: hic, haec, hoc — this; horum, of these (n. gen. pl., partitive: 'of these things')
iaceant: iaceō, -ēre, iacuī — to lie, lie fallen (3rd pl. pres. subj., indirect question)
iapygis: Iāpyx, -ygis (m.) — Iapyx, eponym of Iapygia, the south-eastern Italian heel (m. gen. sg., with agrīs)
idomenei: Īdomeneus, -eī (m.) — Idomeneus, king of Crete, exiled after Troy (gen. sg., Greek form -ēī)
impensis: impēnsa, -ae (f.) — expense, outlay, cost (abl. pl.; tantōrum impēnsīs operum, 'at the cost of so great labours')
implent: impleō, -ēre, -plēvī, -plētum — to fill, fill up (3rd pl. pres.)
importunum: importūnus, -a, -um — unsuitable, harsh, cruel (n. nom. sg., with bellum)
inachias: Īnachius, -a, -um — of Inachus, Argive, Greek (f. acc. pl., with urbēs; Inachus was Argos's river-god)
incuso: incūsō, -āre — to blame, accuse, reproach (1st sg. pres.)
infandae: infandus, -a, -um — unspeakable, abominable (f. gen. sg., with coniugis)
insignes: īnsignis, -e — marked, distinguished, conspicuous (m. nom. pl.)
intulerint: īnferō, -ferre, -tulī, illātum — to carry in; bellum īnferre, make war on (3rd pl. perf. subj., indirect question)
invictisque: invictus, -a, -um — unconquered, unbeaten (m. abl. pl., with virīs) + -que, and
invidisse: invideō, -ēre, -vīdī, -vīsum — to begrudge, envy (+ dat.) (perf. inf., exclamatory: 'did the gods begrudge...?')
lacrimosis: lacrimōsus, -a, -um — tearful, mournful, causing tears (f. abl. pl., with vōcibus)
laetorve: laetor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to rejoice, take pleasure in (+ abl.) (1st sg. pres., deponent) + -ve, or
libycone: Libycus, -a, -um — Libyan, of Libya (n./m. abl. sg., with lītore) + -ne, enclitic question marker
locros: Locrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Locrians, people of Locris (Ajax son of Oileus's men; also their Italian colony Locri) (acc. pl.)
longus: longus, -a, -um — long, extensive (m. nom. sg., with ager)
lugeret: lūgeō, -ēre, lūxī — to mourn, lament, grieve for (3rd sg. impf. subj., in a contrary-to-fact apodosis)
militia: mīlitia, -ae (f.) — military service, campaign, war (abl. sg.; ex illā mīlitiā, 'from that war')
miseranda: miserandus, -a, -um — pitiable, deserving pity (gerundive as adj., f. nom. sg., with manus)
mitto: mittō, -ere, mīsī, missum — to send; here to let go, pass over, leave aside (1st sg. pres.)
motus: mōtus, -ūs (m.) — movement, commotion, disturbance, upheaval (acc. pl.)
murmur: murmur, -uris (n.) — murmur, rumble, low roar (nom. sg.)
mycenaeus: Mycēnaeus, -a, -um — of Mycenae, Mycenaean (m. nom. sg., with ductor; here Agamemnon, king of Mycenae)
navalia: nāvālis, -e — of ships; nāvālia (n. pl.), dockyards, shipbuilding gear, naval stores (n. acc. pl.)
oppetiit: oppetō, -ere, -īvī/-iī, -ītum — to go to meet, meet (death), die (3rd sg. perf., = oppetīvit)
perculsa: percellō, -ere, -culī, -culsum — to strike down, shatter, overthrow (perf. pass. part., n. nom. pl.)
petendum: petō, -ere, -īvī, -ītum — to seek, ask for (gerundive, n. nom. sg., 'to be sought', est understood)
petierunt: petō, -ere, -īvī, -ītum — to seek, make for, reach (3rd pl. perf., = petīvērunt)
placati: plācō, -āre — to calm, soothe, appease (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
pluris: plūs, plūris — more; plūrēs, plūra, more, several (m./f. acc. pl., -is for -ēs, with nāvīs)
ponite: pōnō, -ere, posuī, positum — to put, lay down, set aside (pl. imper.)
portantis: portō, -āre — to carry, bring (pres. part., m. acc. pl., -is for -ēs, with ōrātōrēs)
portatis: portō, -āre — to carry, bring (2nd pl. pres.)
possuntque: possum, posse, potuī — to be able, can (3rd pl. pres.) + -que, and
praecipiant: praecipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to take beforehand; prescribe, lay down, give orders (3rd pl. pres. subj., jussive)
praefatus: praefor, -fārī, -fātus sum — to speak first, say beforehand; praefātus dīvōs, 'having addressed the gods' (perf. part., m. nom. sg.)
praestantibus: praestō, -āre, -stitī — to stand out; praestāns, -antis, outstanding, excellent (pres. part., n. abl. pl., with armīs)
protei: Prōteus, -eī (m.) — Proteus, sea-god and shape-changer of Egypt (gen. sg., Greek form; Prōteī columnae, the Egyptian coast)
rapidos: rapidus, -a, -um — swift, tearing, rushing (m. acc. pl., with amnīs)
recentes: recēns, -entis — fresh, new, newly made (m./f. nom. pl., with tumulī)
referam: referō, -ferre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back, recount (1st sg. pres. subj., deliberative: 'am I to tell...?')
referant: referō, -ferre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back, report, tell (3rd pl. pres. subj., indirect question)
rutulique: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Rutulians, Turnus's people (nom. pl.) + -que, and
sellam: sella, -ae (f.) — seat, chair; sella rēgnī, throne of royal power (acc. sg.)
serunt: serō, -ere, sēvī, satum — to sow, plant (3rd pl. pres.)
siquam: sī quis, sī qua — if any; siquam (f. acc. sg., indef. after sī, with spem)
speranda: spērō, -āre — to hope for, expect (gerundive, n. nom. pl., 'things to be expected', with fuērunt)
statuisse: statuō, -ere, -uī, -ūtum — to set up, resolve, decide, settle (perf. inf., with summā dē rē)
stetimus: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (1st pl. perf.)
suadetque: suādeō, -ēre, suāsī, suāsum — to urge, advise, persuade (3rd sg. pres.) + -que, and
succurrite: succurrō, -ere, -currī, -cursum — to run to help, come to the aid of (+ dat.) (pl. imper.)
texamus: texō, -ere, -uī, textum — to weave, build, construct (1st pl. pres. subj., jussive)
torqueat: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl, hurl (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question)
trabeamque: trabea, -ae (f.) — striped robe of state, royal or consular garment (acc. sg.) + -que, and
valuisse: valeō, -ēre, -uī — to be strong, avail, have power (perf. inf.; nec valuisse, 'had not prevailed')
variusque: varius, -a, -um — varied, diverse, shifting (m. nom. sg., with fremor) + -que, and
versosque: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, overturn, ruin (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl., with penātēs) + -que, and
vicinaeque: vīcīnus, -a, -um — neighbouring, nearby (f. nom. pl., with rīpae) + -que, and
victi: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer; victī, the conquered (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
viderem: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. impf. subj., in an exclamatory question)
violavi: violō, -āre — to injure, outrage, wound (1st sg. perf., = violāvī)
violavimus: violō, -āre — to injure, outrage, desecrate (1st pl. perf., = violāvimus)
vocemus: vocō, -āre — to call, summon, invite (1st pl. pres. subj., jussive)

__broaden__.maesti: maestus, -a, -um — sad, sorrowful, mourning (m. nom. pl.) · also m. gen. sg. (maestī Diomēdis)
__broaden__.saturnia: Sāturnius, -a, -um — of Saturn; Sāturnia, daughter of Saturn, Juno (f. nom. sg.) · also n. nom./acc. pl. (Sāturnia rēgna)

__broaden__.premat: premō, premere, pressī, pressum — to press, bear down on, hold in subjection (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive) · also in a relative clause (quōs Simoīs premat, 'whom Simois overwhelms')
